racePlan.sharpnessHelp: Race sharpness shows whether a rider has enough recent racing rhythm. Higher sharpness helps a rider start sharper and perform more reliably.
racePlan.fatigueHelp: Fatigue is still the main limiter. A rider with good race sharpness but very high fatigue will not start the race fully fresh.
racePlan.freshnessBarHelp: The race-start red freshness bar combines fatigue and race sharpness. It is capped between 50 and 100 so no selected rider starts a race unrealistically empty.

bonus.title: Race Plan Bonus Preview
bonus.description: Race staff, race assets, and team policies are converted into these standardized race-engine percentage bonuses. Hover or click a card to see the source breakdown.
bonus.breakdownHelp: Helpful effects are converted into positive standardized contribution percentages.
bonus.capHelp: If these two numbers differ later, the race engine cap or standardization rule has limited the final bonus.
bonus.noBreakdown: No detailed source rows are available for this bonus yet. Team Policy rows appear only when the current policy setup gives a non-zero bonus.
bonus.none: No standardized race bonuses available yet. Refresh the quote after selecting race staff and race assets.
bonus.fatigueDesc: Reduces race fatigue pressure, travel fatigue, and fatigue floor effects.
bonus.recoveryDesc: Improves daily recovery, recovery duration, and post-stage recovery.
bonus.healthDesc: Reduces injury risk, illness risk, and minor health problems.
bonus.mechanicalDesc: Reduces mechanical problems, mechanical time loss, and equipment-related race issues.
bonus.raceSupportDesc: Improves feeding, team-car coverage, race logistics, and tactical support.

riderRoles.teamLeaderDesc: Main protected rider for the general classification and the rider teammates should protect during key race moments.
riderRoles.sprinterDesc: Primary rider for flat sprint finishes and suitable intermediate sprint opportunities.
riderRoles.climberDesc: Primary rider for difficult climbs, mountain finishes and suitable KOM opportunities.
riderRoles.helperDesc: General support rider who protects teammates, carries out team work and assists with positioning or pace control.
riderRoles.breakawayRiderDesc: Rider selected to attack or join a breakaway when an individual phase instruction allows it.
riderRoles.breakawayChaserDesc: Rider selected to help close dangerous breakaways and support peloton pursuit work.
riderRoles.freeRoleDesc: Neutral role without a fixed team duty. The rider follows phase instructions and reacts to the race situation.

tactics.balancedDesc: Default all-round plan. The team rides with normal energy use, reacts to the race, and does not overcommit too early.
tactics.aggressiveDesc: Higher-rhythm plan. Riders attack, chase and position more actively, but the team will usually spend more stamina.
tactics.sprintControlDesc: The team focuses on controlling the race for a sprint finish, protecting the sprinter, and organizing the sprint train.
tactics.breakawayDesc: The team gives more freedom to breakaway riders and spends less effort on pure sprint control unless the race situation changes.
tactics.gcProtectionDesc: Main focus is keeping the Team Leader safe, protected and well-positioned while avoiding unnecessary risks and fatigue.
tactics.climberSupportDesc: The team puts more support into climbs, mountain pacing and KOM/GC support on uphill sections.
tactics.ttBalancedDesc: Even effort across the whole stage. Safe default with low blow-up risk.
tactics.ttFastStartDesc: Hard first half, then hold the pace. Good for short prologues, risky for weaker TT riders.
tactics.ttNegativeSplitDesc: Controlled first half, stronger second half. Good for longer ITTs and riders with endurance.
tactics.ttAllOutDesc: Maximum pace from the start. Fastest option but high fatigue and blow-up risk.
